body: Please ensure this and other dock PRs are backwards compatible. The 4.6 dock rewrite wasn't and caused months of problems because of it. Please test with Terrain3D.

This feature is insanely good. The amount of customizable and organizable docks would work really well for a music composition software/game.

I believe this feature would benefit a lot if changing layouts were a bit easier. Right now, it takes 3 clicks: Editor -> Editor Layout -> Layout, and there isn't a way to set up shortcuts for that. Shortcuts are only available for saving and deleting layouts. Having shortcuts for switching layouts would allow for much faster context switching.

Another useful addition would be the ability to export the layout .cfg, so people working on the same project could share it, save it in the project, or keep it in an external repository.

I'm a nobody, so feel free to disregard my opinion if it sounds dumb.

> The 4.6 dock rewrite wasn't and caused months of problems because of it.

What were the incompatibilities? They weren't expected, are there any issues open?

Everything has been addressed. The dock changes required me to make a duplicate asset dock and rewrite it. We now have a version that works with 4.5, and one that works with 4.6+.

https://github.com/TokisanGames/Terrain3D/issues/921

We don't join your dev meetings, so everything is a negative surprise. You guys break something, merge it, ship it, and we discover it 6 months later when it's already set in stone. We couldn't support 4.6 until 4.6.3.

I checked the PR for that issue and it seems like your plugin was using some unsupported/undocumented features (e.g. moving between side docks and bottom wasn't exposed before). In that case the incompatibilities were actually expected. We don't give any guarantee about anything that isn't part of the public API, if you are using hacks they may break at any point.

That said, this PR does not change anything fundamental about the dock system. It mostly changes global node paths to docks.

We were using supported, documented features that were instantly retired, marked deprecated but without backwards compatibility or transition period. 

Moving docks between sidebars and the bottom absolutely was exposed and documented. We've been using it for years and learned about it from the documentation. 
 
Everything we've done in the engine is publicly exposed. We couldn't do anything with something not exposed. 

We had to make some of our own features due to a severe lack of functionality. These were the easiest to fix once that functionality was built in.

The bottom line is my request remains to do more testing, since there have been multiple dock PRs. This one may not change the API, but your other one does, and I don't know how many others there have been or will come out in 4.7.

Had there been more testing in 4.6, rather than the rush release, backwards compatibility or a workaround could have been built in. Instead hundreds of early adopters used a broken system for four months until we could finally address all issues. The dock issues were only a small portion of 4.6 problems. Thank you.

Tried this PR and it's looking pretty good! Some findings:

- The layout was totally borked upon opening the editor. You mentioned that compatibility code might be difficult, but... I fear this needs something – be it backward compatibility, or just a reset-to-default + a big announcement when this gets merged.

- The small layout in the context menu of tabs is totally borked with this PR. Panels are in positions not present in the small layout, the panel counts in the layout are inaccurate, and position previews are broken. Time to yeet it?

- The final drop in the video below is unexpected. I said this before and I know you didn't like my suggestion back then but I think this can only be solved with an additional bottom margin that creates a preview that runs across all the columns, and which should also be triggerable from any of the columns.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/763572b4-9e0d-4081-86bc-b4a68d56a482

- It seems like the final drop behavior in the video above only applies to the left side and not the right side of the window.

- It seems I can't further horizontally split the extended bottom panels... which is probably fine. The rules for this are very opaque, which may prove to be confusing to users, but idk.

I resolved the layout problem by adding versioning to the layouts. So besides that, I didn't encounter any bugs, and this is a desirable feature. I will point out how squeezed the new docks start as, especially since dragging the horizontal handle doesn't move neighboring docks to the side in order to expand them.

> dragging the horizontal handle doesn't move neighboring docks to the side in order to expand them.

Soo 💀
This is a result of changing the side docks to use separate split containers, to allow having multi-column docks. It was working fine before.

[Nagranie ekranu_20260904_142300.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b1eacbb4-c776-4c3a-9166-ed8f53379bf6)

The split container would need to be able to push other containers to fix it.

I can fix the width of newly added docks, but it's going to be a bit hacky.
I added some extra space to new columns, so you can drag the handles a bit.

> I added some extra space to new columns, so you can drag the handles a bit.

I'm not really seeing a difference?

> The split container would need to be able to push other containers to fix it.

Not saying this should be done in this PR, but it's a big paper cut for it to not work like that anymore, especially for a feature like this. I think it's worth some hackiness to bring it back.
Eh, would it be fine to leave the size as-is, if the docks could be pushed like before? I'm removing the multi-column slots, because they are not worth the hassle.
It would be a pity, since multi columns are a feature people seem to crave. But you're in charge of this PR, so it's your call.
By multi-column I mean https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/10005, the extra columns are still going to be supported.
Oh, I see. While also nice, that is far less of a deal breaker. So yes, the size issue would be easier to ignore if the docks could be pushed around by dragging.
